9:["$","ul","2",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Ulnar deviation</strong> — your hands angle outward from the wrist toward your pinkies because a standard keyboard is narrower than your shoulders. This compresses the ulnar nerve and tightens the forearm extensors."}}],["$","li","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Pronation</strong> — your forearm rotates so your palms face down, even though the relaxed neutral position is a \"handshake\" angle. Sustained pronation strains the radial nerve and the muscles between the elbow and wrist."}}]]}]
a:["$","p","3",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Over years, those two compounding strains produce the symptoms most desk workers eventually develop: tingling fingers, sore forearms, weakness gripping objects, and the diagnosis nobody wants — <strong>carpal tunnel syndrome</strong> or <strong>tennis elbow</strong> from typing. The fix isn't a wrist rest. It's a keyboard built to put your hands in a natural position from minute one."}}]
b:["$","p","4",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"This is the <strong>best ergonomic keyboard for wrist pain</strong> guide for 2026 — six options across price tiers, plus what to look for and what to skip."}}]
c:["$","h2","5",{"id":"what-makes-a-keyboard-ergonomic","children":"What Makes a Keyboard Ergonomic"}]
d:["$","p","6",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Marketing puts \"ergonomic\" on every product. Three criteria actually matter for wrist pain relief:"}}]
e:["$","ul","7",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Split design</strong> — the keyboard separates into two halves you can position at shoulder width. Eliminates ulnar deviation completely. The single most important feature."}}],["$","li","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Tenting (tilt)</strong> — the inner edges of each half rise so your palms angle slightly inward. Reduces pronation. Look for <strong>adjustable tenting from 0° to at least 30°.</strong>"}}],["$","li","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Negative tilt</strong> — the back edge sits lower than the front, opposite of laptop keyboards. Lets your wrists stay neutral instead of bending backward."}}],["$","li","3",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Mechanical key switches</strong> — Cherry MX, Kailh, or similar tactile switches require less force than membrane keyboards (45-60g vs 70g+). Less force = less repetitive strain."}}],["$","li","4",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Thumb keys</strong> — relocating frequently-used keys (Backspace, Enter, Space, Cmd) to dedicated thumb-cluster positions takes load off the weak pinky finger and onto the strongest digit."}}]]}]
f:["$","p","8",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Of these, <strong>split + tenting</strong> is non-negotiable for genuine wrist pain relief. Anything missing both is just a curved-shape regular keyboard."}}]

2b:["$","ul","36",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Days 1-3:</strong> Typing speed drops 40-60%. Errors spike. Don't quit. This is normal."}}],["$","li","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Days 4-10:</strong> Muscle memory begins to form. Errors decrease faster than speed recovers."}}],["$","li","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Days 11-21:</strong> Most users hit 80% of their old typing speed."}}],["$","li","3",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Day 22 onward:</strong> Speed matches or exceeds the old keyboard. Wrist pain symptoms typically begin improving in this window."}}],["$","li","4",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>2-3 months:</strong> Full adaptation. Going back to a flat keyboard feels uncomfortable."}}]]}]
2c:["$","p","37",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"If you're still slower than your old keyboard after 6 weeks, you likely have the wrong layout for your hands. Switch to a different model — flat-shaped split (K860) is easier to adapt to than concave-well (Kinesis)."}}]
2d:["$","h2","38",{"id":"other-things-that-help-wrist-pain","children":"Other Things That Help Wrist Pain"}]
2e:["$","p","39",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"A keyboard alone won't solve wrist pain if other ergonomic basics are wrong. Pair it with:"}}]
2f:["$","ul","40",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"A <strong>proper desk and chair height</strong> so your forearms stay parallel to the floor — see our <a href=\"/blog/ergonomic-home-office-setup-guide\" class=\"text-orange-600 dark:text-orange-400 hover:underline font-medium\">ergonomic home office setup guide</a>"}}],["$","li","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"A <strong>vertical mouse</strong> to address pronation on the right hand — see our <a href=\"/blog/best-vertical-mouse-for-wrist-pain-2026\" class=\"text-orange-600 dark:text-orange-400 hover:underline font-medium\">best vertical mouse for wrist pain guide</a>"}}],["$","li","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Hourly micro-breaks</strong> with 30 seconds of wrist circles, finger stretches, and forearm extensions"}}],["$","li","3",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Wrist rests in front of the keyboard</strong> (gel or memory foam) so wrists don't bend backward"}}],["$","li","4",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"A <strong>chair with armrests at the right height</strong> — see <a href=\"/blog/best-office-chair-lower-back-pain-2026\" class=\"text-orange-600 dark:text-orange-400 hover:underline font-medium\">best office chair for lower back pain</a>, which also covers armrest height for arm support"}}]]}]
30:["$","h2","41",{"id":"what-to-skip","children":"What to Skip"}]
31:["$","ul","42",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>\"Ergonomic\" keyboards that are just curved one-piece units without splitting.</strong> A curved shape doesn't fix ulnar deviation — only true splitting does. Logitech K860 is the exception (the curve is wide enough to function as a split)."}}],["$","li","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Cheap split keyboards under $50.</strong> Build quality is poor, switches die quickly, and the layout often makes typing slower without actually fixing ergonomics."}}],["$","li","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Apple Magic Keyboard.</strong> Aesthetic but ergonomically inferior — flat profile + narrow form factor causes ulnar deviation."}}]]}]
32:["$","h2","43",{"id":"frequently-asked-questions","children":"Frequently Asked Questions"}]
33:["$","p","44",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Will an ergonomic keyboard cure my wrist pain?</strong>"}}]
34:["$","p","45",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"For most users with mild-to-moderate RSI from typing, yes — symptoms substantially improve within 3-6 weeks of consistent use. For diagnosed carpal tunnel or severe tendonitis, the keyboard is part of treatment, not a cure. Pair with a doctor's visit."}}]
35:["$","p","46",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>How much should I spend on an ergonomic keyboard?</strong>"}}]
36:["$","p","47",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"For most desk workers, the Logitech K860 at $130 captures 70% of the benefit. For severe RSI, the Kinesis Advantage 360 at $449 is worth every dollar — it's the keyboard that changes lives."}}]
37:["$","p","48",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Are split keyboards good for gaming?</strong>"}}]
38:["$","p","49",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Mostly no. The unconventional layouts hurt twitch reaction time. Stick with a regular mechanical for gaming and use the ergonomic split for typing-heavy work."}}]
39:["$","p","50",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>How long does it take to type as fast on an ergonomic keyboard?</strong>"}}]
3a:["$","p","51",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Most users hit 80% speed within 2 weeks and full speed within 4-6 weeks. The Kinesis Advantage takes longer (4-6 weeks for 80%, 2-3 months for full speed) due to its concave wells."}}]
3b:["$","p","52",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Can I use an ergonomic keyboard with a laptop?</strong>"}}]
3c:["$","p","53",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Yes — pair it with a <a href=\"/blog/best-laptop-stand\" class=\"text-orange-600 dark:text-orange-400 hover:underline font-medium\">laptop stand</a> to raise the screen to eye level. The laptop keyboard becomes obsolete; you type on the external keyboard instead."}}]
3d:["$","p","54",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>What's the difference between mechanical and membrane in ergonomic keyboards?</strong>"}}]
3e:["$","p","55",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Mechanical switches require less force per keystroke and provide tactile feedback that reduces \"bottoming out\" — both reduce strain. Membrane is fine for casual use but mechanical is meaningfully better for 4+ hour daily typing."}}]
